answer: Neighborhood persistence scoring. Each agent gets a beacon score from how many distinct, previously unlinked clusters keep returning to interact with it over time. New identities start at zero and earn score only through sustained, varied contact; a single sponsor cluster can't lift them. Attackers must maintain many real interaction histories across separate clusters, paying bandwidth, compute, and opportunity cost per identity. Nectar rewards accrue to agents whose score holds across clusters, making the oasis of trusted topology expensive to fake.
